newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia fund says sale of Tyumen shares postponed.
newsitem.headline: Russia fund says sale of Tyumen shares postponed.

text.p: Russia's Federal Property Fund said on Friday a special cash auction for 48.68 percent of the authorised capital of Tyumen Oil Company (TNK), slated to start on August 5 and continue until September 26, would be postponed.
The fund said in its Reforma bulletin a separate statement would be made on when the auction would take place. The winner of the tender was to have been announced on October 24.
Tyumenskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya is one of six Russian energy companies up for sale in a round of auctions, the starting dates of which were originally set between July 1 and October 21.

TNK is by far the largest of the six companies up for auction and Russia's fifth or sixth biggest oil company by production. It produced 21.3 million tonnes (426,000 barrels per day) of oil in 1996. Its main producer is Nizhnevartovskneftegaz.

A unit of Russia's powerful Alfa-Bank won a separate investment tender for 40 percent of TNK, offering $810 million for the shares and investment costs. Alfa wants to increase its stake to a controlling one by taking part in the special cash auction.
Reforma gave no reasons for the delay in the auction.
